notes: The date names Darius’s second year, the sixth month, and its first day. Zerubbabel’s governorship and Joshua’s priesthood remain distinct.
The repeated call to consider their ways links daily frustration with the neglected house; the repetition is intentional.
vocabulary: Zerubbabel’s civil office, distinct from the high priest’s role.
An expression for awakening resolve to act.

notes: The Hebrew has a plural coming verb with the nations’ desirable things or treasures; the draft does not turn this into a single person’s title.
The priests distinguish the transfer of holiness from the transfer of uncleanness. These are ritual categories within the analogy.
The repeated “from this day” marks a turning point. Verse 16 does not identify the unit behind the first quantity; “measures” leaves the unit unspecified.
vocabulary: Shalom includes well-being and wholeness, beyond the absence of conflict.
A seal associated with a bearer’s identity and authority.
